newsitem.title: USA: Ashland off to "reasonable start" in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ashland off to "reasonable start" in 1997.

text.p: Ashland Inc is off to a "reasonable start" operationally in 1997 and is continuing to pursue its profitability improvement plan, chief executive Paul Chellgren said.
"We remain optimistic that fiscal 1997 will be a year of growth and progress for Ashland," Chellgren added.

He said Ashland is making progress under the profitability improvement plan announced last month, noting it has established a new Petroleum Group consisting of Ashland Petroleum, SuperAmerica and Valvoline that reports to group operating officer J.A. "Fred" Brothers.
Noting the limit of $100 million placed on capital expenditures for refining in fiscal 1997, ending September 30, Chellgren said these outlays totaled $21 million for the December quarter.
He said a team of senior employees is working with outside advisors, continuing the review of options for strategic alliances for Ashland's refining and marketing operations.
"It is too early to predict the outcome of these efforts. However, Ashland remains committed to actively pursuing this initiative to improve returns from refining and marketing," Chellgren said.
He noted Ashland Chemical closed six acquisitions during the quarter as it continues to expand distribution and specialty chemical businesses in the United States and abroad.
The chemical company also announced a 115,000-square-foot expansion of its Dublin, Ohio, technical center to provide technical support for continued growth.
Chellgren said Valvoline Instant Oil Change entered a retail partnership with Sears, Roebuck and Co to set up shop in 20 Sears Auto Centers in Dallas, Minneapolis/St. Paul and Kansas City.
The three markets will serve as tests in anticipation of opening VIOC service centers in more than 150 Sears Auto Centers nationwide over the next three years.

He said no stock purchases have occurred as a result of a plan, approved in December, to repurchase up to one million common shares to help offset dilution due to company benefit programs. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
